title: Search Insert Position
prompt: Given a sorted array of distinct integers `nums` and a `target` value, return the index if `target` is found. If not, return the index where it would be inserted to keep `nums` sorted. Your algorithm must run in `O(log n)` time.

examples.explanation: 2 isn't in the array, but inserting it at index 1 keeps nums sorted: [1,2,3,5,6].
7 is larger than every element, so it belongs at the end.

constraints: nums contains distinct values sorted in ascending order
hints: A linear scan to find the first element >= target works in O(n), but the sorted array supports something faster.
Binary search for the leftmost position where target could be inserted without breaking the ordering.
Track the smallest index seen so far where nums[mid] >= target; when the search space is exhausted, that index (or one past the end if never found) is the answer.

solution.approach: Binary search for the first index where nums[mid] >= target. Each time nums[mid] is at least target, that index is a candidate insertion point, so record it and search left for an even earlier one; otherwise the insertion point must be to the right, so search right. When low and high cross, low is exactly the number of elements smaller than target, which is both the correct index if target exists and the correct insertion point if it doesn't.
